title: Douglas v. Deutsche Bank National Trust Co., No. 24-CV-1099, Published Order

reading.body:
This is a case of a model asserting something false as fact, and that false content reaching a formal legal proceeding. A court in the District of Columbia faulted lawyers for a Deutsche Bank subsidiary over an AI hallucination, according to the reporting. The failure did not stay in a draft or a private workspace, it entered a court filing made in the name of counsel.

The point of failure sits at the drafting of a legal submission, a step where a professional is expected to verify what goes out under their name. Catching it would have taken a person checking the AI-supplied content against the underlying record before the document was filed. The court placed the fault with the lawyers rather than with the tool.

What is not established here is the substance of the order. The second report is the order itself, and the summary available describes only a corrupted file that could not be read, so the specific false statement and the court's reasoning are not known from this material. A court faulting lawyers is a finding by that court, not proof of intent.
